idea: Why a toilet may keep running
title: Why Your Toilet Keeps Running (And How to Spot the Cause)
description: A continuously running toilet is more than an annoying sound—it can waste hundreds of gallons of clean water every day. Most running issues originate inside the porcelain cistern from three common culprits. First, a degraded rubber flapper may no longer create a watertight seal, letting water constantly trickle into the bowl. Second, a float height set too high allows water to continuously spill over the top of the vertical overflow tube. Finally, an aging fill valve may simply fail to shut off. Inspecting inside the tank is your best first step. If basic adjustments don't solve it, a licensed plumber can efficiently replace the worn internal components.
image_prompt: A professional high-detail vertical 9:16 photograph taken inside a bright modern residential bathroom, looking down into an open white ceramic toilet tank with its lid removed and resting neatly alongside. The tank is filled with clear, still water. Inside the tank, realistic internal components are clearly visible in sharp focus: a modern fill valve on the left with a vertical float adjustment stem, a central open overflow tube, and a dark flexible rubber flapper sitting flush over the drain opening at the bottom. A gentle trickle of water is visible just over the top lip of the overflow tube. Crisp interior lighting creates realistic reflections on the water surface and highlights the matte texture of the plastic components and smooth glazed porcelain.
